findings.where: First screen, the action row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one job is getting in touch, and the hero action that should do it does nothing. 'Write to me' looks like a primary button and has a hover rule, but it is not a link or a button. The underlined address next to it is also plain text. The only working mailto is the small footer link at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who decides to contact Mark clicks the obvious blue button or the underlined address, and nothing happens. Some will give up there. Few will scroll past a whole style tile to find the footer address.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Book a consultation' next to 'Write to me'
findings.fault: The hero has two equal filled blue buttons, so it does not have one action. 'Book a consultation' goes to #consult, and the page has no consultation section, so the one button that acts goes nowhere. 'Booking' also promises a scheduling service Mark does not offer. It reads like a sales funnel, not a personal advisor.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark and warns against salesy copy. The visitor faces two equal choices, and the one that works lands nowhere.

findings.where: First screen, the three margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024); the same blue sans also on every specimen label (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: Static text is set in the house blue, which the palette swatch itself names as the colour of links and the action. The margin notes are named talk titles, so they look and read like links to those talks, but they are not clickable. The site's link colour now means two things.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to read the Istanbul or Melbourne talk clicks its title and gets nothing. They then stop trusting blue as the sign of a link anywhere else on the site. This clashes with the brief's 'small blue sans margin notes', so it goes to the founder.

findings.where: First screen ground: the pale blue-to-lilac gradient behind the hero
findings.fault: The hero sits on a cool blue-to-lavender gradient, not the warm paper. Lavender is not a house colour, and the gradient is a second ground and an extra hue. The tile's own palette and texture sections promise 'three colours, no accent' and 'a flat warm tone', so the first screen contradicts the system shown below it. The gradient also gives the hero a generic tech-product look.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft ground, the house blue and grey as the only ink, and nothing 'in-your-face techy'. A visitor gets a SaaS-landing-page impression, not a legal journal.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph 'I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…' (worst on the phone, eight lines of capitals)
findings.fault: The sentence that says what Mark does and for whom is set in widely tracked bold capitals. That makes it the slowest text on the page to read, and it shouts like a corporate label instead of sounding like a person speaking. In weight it competes with the heading and outranks the serif paragraph under it.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for who he is and who he serves stumbles over a block of capitals. The founder asked for serious type, his voice rather than a label, and a look not owned by any consultancy.

findings.fault: The address is squeezed between the two buttons with almost no space above or below. 'Book a consultation' is indented from the left edge that everything else shares. The group reads as stacked by accident rather than as one contact.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor, likely arriving from LinkedIn, sees a ragged, crowded contact area at the very point where they decide whether to write.

findings.where: Header nav: Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog
findings.fault: The nav links jump to #profile, #articles and #blog, but no such sections are visible on the page, so on this tile they lead nowhere. There is also no Contact item.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who opens 'Articles and Presentations' to check Mark's work lands on nothing and loses the proof the brief calls the product.

findings.where: Header, the logo lockup on desktop
findings.fault: The 'MMM INFRA' lettering under the arches sits right on the header band's bottom edge, where the hero gradient begins. The mark has almost no clear space and looks clipped.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, for whom the logo is the brand's anchor. It reads as cramped at the first thing a visitor sees.

findings.where: Article specimen, the outlined pill 'Download' button, against the square-cornered filled hero buttons
findings.fault: The page's two actions use unrelated button shapes: square-cornered filled rectangles in the hero, a rounded pill outline in the document row. Like parts are not treated alike.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who needs one button style to reuse when she adds content. A careful reader notices the inconsistency.

findings.where: Motion sketch, desktop: the curve, the exhibit photo and the table
findings.fault: The exhibit photo floats at the right, aligned to neither the text column nor the table below it, and a large empty area opens under the curve on the left. The section looks unarranged next to the strict column grid above it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the specimen parts. The loose grid undercuts the 'well-set brief' idea of this direction.
